_help.about: (design §FE) What lurks in a ruin's dark, below its one boss (§EY.1 stays): each ruin kind has its own plan and its own residents, and each creature its own algorithm (Mike, 6 Oct, 22:32). The creatures and their 'mike' lines are Mike's; ranks, answers, tells and every number are Claude (chat)'s first guesses, 6 Oct night. Speeds in m/s: the ambient walk is 4.3, the sprint 5.6 (movement.json profiles.ambient). §FJ.2 (Mike, 22:52): the desert tomb's mummy, waking in its sarcophagus (rank and numbers Claude's first guesses). Wired for the skeleton (Claude Code, 7 Oct, queue 58; scripts/crawler/residents.gd, resident.gd): what a resident senses (notice), its chase (gives_up: Pursuit, queue 56) and its strike (strike: CreatureStrike, queue 57, with the torch's stagger) are shared by every creature; the one algorithm built is the creeper's (Mike, 7 Oct, amending §FE.2's waker for the skeleton: pattern creeper, its creep block, see _help.skeleton_creep; with rise_s, walk_mps, eye_m; it always walks home to rest, returns_to_rest), and a creature with no creep block runs the waker's (pattern waker: wakes_m), and its two tells are the skeleton's own sounds (near: bone grinding, SoundSynth bone_grind; wind_up: the jaw's creak and knock, strike.sound jaw_creak, with the jaw open on its sprite); the tomb's generator lays the skeletons (skeleton_built). [NOT WIRED YET — design §FE.2, §FJ.2] the ghost, the temple cat, the zombie, the were-mole and the mummy wait for their worlds; fire_hp and oil_scale are wired for the skeleton (Claude Code, 7 Oct, queue 60: FirePots' fire-target socket; a pot burns fire_hp down times oil_scale, at 0 it burns out and is gone, burnt asleep it wakes, awake it sees the lit wick and hears the burst). retreat_to is wired for the skeleton (queue 59, §FF.2: back_into_its_niche, back into its own niche or grave, or a nearer one left open; since Mike's note of 7 Oct it walks there, climbs in and lies down as bones for good, never sinking into the stone); the other creatures' wait with them. Mike's note of 7 Oct: 'creatures shouldnt "sink" into the stone- only ghosts/phantoms should have the ability to ohase thru walls and floors and ceilings': nothing here goes into the stone, vanishes or comes up elsewhere; the ghost's through_walls is the one exception, not built.
_help.rules: §FD, §FF.2. gives_up: the ways a chase can end; each creature lists its own. chase_enters_light: a creature that has hit you may follow you into lit rooms (§FD, amends §EY.1 for chases); back_to_dark_s: once it gives you up in the light, how long before it is gone back into the dark. retreat_on_floor_lit: a floor with every light relit is cleared; its residents leave by retreat_to, seen going (§FF.2). pocket_counterattack_m: on a half-lit floor they fall back into dark pockets and strike at anyone who comes within this (§FF.2). light_heals: false (§FD, Mike). Wired for the residents (queue 58, through queue 56's Pursuit): gives_up, each creature's own mix (distance_m: past it the chase ends at once; out_of_sight_s: it hasn't seen you, your light or heard you that long; hide: true when being out of its sight line behind low cover hides you, false when it finds you behind cover; torch_doused: true when smothering your torch ends the chase at once); light_heals false (harm.json fd.recover_starts: you heal only once nothing is pursuing you). Wired for the residents by queue 59 (§FF.2; Claude Code, 7 Oct; Residents, Resident, on queue 49's graph of the tomb's rooms and corridor stretches, lit or dark), and amended by Mike's note of 7 Oct ('creatures that are actively chasing will chase near the fire but stay somewhat in the darkness if they can- they may show just enough of their face/body near the fire'): chase_enters_light now means a chase comes toward the light, its strike landed or not, only as far as its edge: chase_light_cap (Claude Code's first guess): a chasing creature, the snake too, stands only where the light on the floor (crawler.json light_field, the renderer's own light units) is at most this, about 5.5 m from a corridor's torch, 6 m from a room's and 7 m from the hearth; it watches you from that edge for edge_watch_s, then gives you up; it strikes only if you are within its reach of where it may stand, so by a fire you are safe from it and at the light's dim edge you are not. One woken where the light passes the cap (its resting place by a relit torch of a half-lit room) climbs out and goes for the dimmest corner of its dark instead, no one's pursuer, and it never springs from there. (Until that note a chase that had hit you followed you into the lit rooms.) back_to_dark_s: relight the room or stretch a resident rests or stands in, or let it give you up in the light, and it goes for the nearest dark by the dimmest way (crawler.json light_field) fast enough to be out of the light this long after it starts (resting, it climbs out first, its near tell heard); given up, it walks home only by a way through the dark to a resting place still dark, else it hangs back in the dark (a dark pocket). Cut off from every dark it could walk to without crossing the lit hearth room (Mike's note of 7 Oct: nothing goes into the stone), it walks out through the light on its dimmest way at its walk_mps to the nearest dark, the hearth room's edges included, only while you can't see it (a creeper), so the floor's residents end up in what dark is left. below_s is no longer read (queue 59 had a cut-off one go into the stone for that long and come up elsewhere). pocket_counterattack_m: one hanging back in a dark pocket strikes when you come this close where it can sense you, lunging in at pocket_lunge_mps as it winds up (its normal strike, so a lit torch's swing in the wind-up staggers it), then hunts you. retreat_on_floor_lit (crawler.json cleared): when the floor's last light catches, every resident leaves by its retreat_to: since Mike's note of 7 Oct it hurries at retreat_mps by the dimmest way to its own niche or grave (or a nearer one left open), climbs in and lies down, and is bones from then on, set dressing for good, never waking (seen or not; one too far off keeps walking there, however long it takes). withdraw_s is no longer read (it sank into the stone over that long). edge_watch_s, pocket_lunge_mps, retreat_mps and chase_light_cap are Claude Code's first guesses; Mike tunes by playing. pocket_counterattack_m 3 to 2 (Mike, 7 Oct, answering the open call on it: "skeletons should lunge at the player within 2 meters"; Claude Code): a dark pocket's skeleton lunges at you within 2 m, as creep.lunge_m does for one up and about.
_help.creatures: §FE.2. Per creature: where (the ruin kind), rank (resident / boss / open), pattern (its algorithm), speeds, notice (sees_flame_m, hears_step_m: how far it sees a carried flame and hears a walking step; a sneak is heard at a tenth, as built), gives_up (its mix of rules.gives_up, with numbers), strike (reach_m, wind_up_s: the window in which a torch swing staggers it, §FA.1), tells (near: the sound it makes about the place; wind_up: its own strike tell, seen head-on or heard when it ambushes, §FA.2), fire_hp (burnt down by fire_pots.json bursts and burn), oil_scale (§FA.3: some oils do more), retreat_to (§FF.2).
_help.skeleton_built: (Claude Code, 7 Oct, queue 58, first guesses; Mike tunes by playing) The tomb's skeletons. per_dungeon: how many a tomb lays [min, max], fewer if it has fewer niches and graves; heart_holds_one: the heart's coffin (Mike's frame 9, the skeleton leaning out of the mossy box) always holds one; toward_heart: a room's draw weight is its depth (rooms from the hearth room) to this power, so more lie toward the heart; none in the hearth room. rests_in: wall_niche is a catacomb shelf stack with a stone frame round it and the middle shelf gone (the skeleton sits hunched on the bottom shelf), grave a crypt coffin with its lid shoved off (it kneels inside, slumped over the end). off_line_m: a resting place keeps this far from the line through the rooms' doors (the way through, §EX.5 until the spine is built); apart_m: two never rest closer than this. eye_m: its eyes standing. notice.sees_you_m: how far it sees you yourself in the dark with a clear line from its eyes to your head (cover breaks it, §FC.2); sees_flame_m: your lit torch's flame, or the stone it lights round you (stealth.json hide.glow_reach_m), with a clear line; hears_step_m: a walking step, scaled by your noise (a sprint, or a swing that lands on a creature, about three times as far; a sneak under a third). strike (queue 57's CreatureStrike, the keys as bosses.json _help.strike): within reach_m, sensing you there, it winds up for wind_up_s (the jaw drops open on its sprite and you hear sound, the jaw's creak and knock, from its first frame; a lit torch swung into it now staggers it, torch.json stagger, and it reels back reel_m); then the committed strike, strike_s, and the hit (harm.json) lands at its end if you are still within reach_m with nothing solid between; recover_s before it can wind up again; body_r: how big a target its head is for a swing. sprite: the baked sheet (§ET.8, eight around by three heights): height_m standing, px a frame's height.
_help.skeleton_creep: (Claude Code, 7 Oct; Claude Code's first guesses on Mike's 7 Oct note, amending §FE.2's 'climb out when you come too close'; Mike tunes by playing) Mike: "for skeletons itd be cool if they acted similar to boos in mario- they might not activate until you pass them once and only move toward you slowly when your back is turned so you never see them moving unless they get right up on you". The skeleton is a creeper (pattern creeper; Resident, Residents.watched). arms_m (replaces the waker's wakes_m for the skeleton, the same 3 m): your head this near its head at rest, with a clear line, arms it, silently; armed, it climbs out the first moment you can't see it, its near tell (bone grinding) heard behind you. creep_mps: how fast it comes for you, hunting (your walk is 4.3; walking home it walks, walk_mps). It moves only unseen: while you can see it, it holds dead still (no step, no turn, no change of pose; a climb or a creep goes on from where it froze), and a step that would leave it in your sight is undone, so it stops just short. You see it when any of its feet, middle and head (as it lies, climbs or stands), or its middle side_m to either side as you see it, is in the frame or within view_margin of its edge (a share of the frame on each side: 0.08 is about 4 degrees past each edge at the crawler's 78-degree view), within seen_m of your eye, with nothing of the stone between; the dark doesn't hide it. Watched it still senses you and keeps its chase (gives_up unchanged), and the light's rules (§FF.2) still say where it may go: it goes for the dark or home only once you look away, and back_to_dark_s counts only the time you aren't watching it. In plain view all the same: its whole strike (wind-up and tell, the strike, the recovery, a stagger's reel, a dark pocket's lunge within rules.pocket_counterattack_m); up and about, anything within lunge_m of you; and the floor's last light, when the ones you can see hurry back to their niches and graves (§FF.2's reveal). lunge_m (Mike, 7 Oct: 'skeletons should lu ge at the player within 2 meters'; it replaces strike.reach_m, 1.6, as the reach inside which it moves in plain view): an awake one within this of you, sensing you, lunges at you in plain view at rules.pocket_lunge_mps as it winds up its strike (the jaw's creak; a lit torch's swing staggers it, §FA.1), to bring you into its reach, and strikes; never past the light's edge (rules.chase_light_cap). A fire pot still wakes one at rest (it burns), but watched it lies there burning until you look away.
